held.why: REFUSED: Doesn't teach the link to the key. It quotes 'must not stay in such a place' (line 72) but stops before 'where he might lose his balance' (line 73), the only words that show he could fall. No sentence connects that reminder to ignoring the dragonfly, so a child is not shown why the key ('reminded that he could fall') is right.

REFUSED: Child-facing form: the last sentence, 'A thing that goes on a head, and it is hers.', is a fragment with no main clause for its first half. It also asserts the hidden thing is worn on the head, which lines 39-41 do not say; the hat only appears at line 42. It also credits the meaning to 'his little nods' alone, where line 41 gives it to the signs and nods together.

REFUSED: Doesn't teach the half of the key the question turns on, 'although his end has none'. It never points to line 33 ('two jumpers and the air between them'), and it never points to the contrast in 'still' on line 34. Lines 36-37, 'nobody has ever said there is not one', are reported without showing that there really is no net.

REFUSED: Wrong line cited. 'Line 65 says look, and be afraid' is wrong, because 'Look, and be' is on line 64 and line 65 holds only 'afraid!'. Also, 'Line 64 tells the story of the mark' is only partly right: the story begins on line 63 ('The great God Brahm put his mark upon all our people').

REFUSED: Misleads. 'Line 38 has Mrs Farrell say the word again.' leaves 'again' unquoted, so it reads as 'says the word a second time' rather than naming the word in the stem. The word itself is on line 39, not line 38. The script also never reaches line 40, 'everybody has moved on from it', which supports 'which he thinks is finished'.

REFUSED: Doesn't teach the 'holds it in' half of the key and risks misleading. The first sentence, 'wanted to lay her head down and cry' (line 39), is the literal-lookalike distractor, and the script never says that she did not cry. 'she winked hard' (line 41) is left unexplained as holding back tears. Lines 40-41 ('tears were an unmanly weakness', 'couldn't quite forgive yet') are skipped.

REFUSED: Doesn't teach the key. 'as a man looks who thinks on flight' (line 54) is the only words that support 'looking for a way out', and the script never explains that 'flight' here means running away. The other evidence it lists, the step trembling and the hand shaking, fits the 'he is ill' distractor just as well, so the script does not separate the key from it.

REFUSED: Leaves out the evidence for the key. The key is 'Something he heard', and it rests on line 45 'He is listening to the door' and line 46 'Oh, hang on'. The script stops at 'then he stops' and never mentions listening. Its only evidence is something passing his ear and him swatting at it, which points the child towards the swatting distractor instead.
